newsitem.title: ITALY: International community pledges to help Albania.
newsitem.headline: International community pledges to help Albania.

text.p: The international community pledged on Thursday to help Albania rebuild itself socially, politically, economically and militarily.

"The international community intends to continue its support of the efforts of Albania towards the normalisation of its internal security and of its economic and social revivial," Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said.
Dini was speaking to reporters during a break in an international donors' conference, called to discuss how to rebuild Albania's shattered economy, the poorest in Europe.

The day-long meeting, attended by delegations from 35 countries and international organisations, will be followed by a larger conference on the future of Albania due to be held in Italy in the autumn.
No financial details were disclosed. The conference was resuming later on Thursday to work out a final document.

"Within the international community there is one opinion, one view, one approach. There are no deviations," said Franz Vranitsky, the mediator for Albania from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

"We will continue to fill the framework with substance with regard to the reconstruction of the Albanian police force, of the army, of commerce, of financial systems and of the constitution," Vranitsky told a news conference.

"This is a comprehensive approach," he said, adding that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank would send teams to Tirana in August to help with economic programmes such as banking systems.
He said the IMF and World Bank would also be involved in compiling statistics on pyramid schemes.

The collapse of shaky investment pyramid schemes earlier this year swallowed the life savings of tens of thousands of Albanians and triggered months of anarchy which led to the fall of the government of former President Sali Berisha.
Vranitsky said the OSCE would establish a civic register and the United States had pledged to help set up an independent media programme in Albania.
Dini confirmed that Italy would leave a residual force in Albania after a 7,000-strong multinational security force currently deployed there completes its withdrawal on August 12.
Italian officials have said previously that the new force will be entrusted with civil duties including including helping train Albanian military and police forces.
Fatos Nano, the new Albanian Prime Minister who triumphed in a recent general election, attended the conference and pronounced himself pleased with the results.
"Our (government) programme has not only received a (parliamentary) vote of confidence but today it has received a vote of confidence from the international community," he said.

Italian foreign ministry officials said Italy and Albania had renewed until October 30 a bilateral agreement that allows the Italian navy to patrol Albanian territorial waters to dissuade Albanians from fleeing across the southern Adriatic.
Italy has borne the brunt of the Albanian crisis. More than 14,000 refugees flooded into Italy earlier this year aboard a flotilla of rusty ships.
